title: Normalized scalar localization
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D with algebraic closure k of a finite field and a coefficient datum C with prime ell different from char(k), a fixed algebraic closure of Q_ell, and its finite intermediate fields E. Let f : X → Y be smooth separated of pure relative dimension d ≥ 0 between separated finite-type k-schemes. Let S be a constructible exceptional coefficient system and I its supplied simultaneous integral purity data [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality]. With Q,T,alpha,unit,tShift of [def-pur-rational-scalar-comparison-data], exist scalar localization isomorphisms C_F/E,W ⋙ Q_F,W ≅ Q_E,W ⋙ T_F/E,W at W=X,Y. Their hom components are heterogeneously equal to Q_F of scalarBridge, they respect the recorded shifts, and T with tShift is triangulated. Localizing the integral scalar unitor equals this identification followed by the rational tensor unitor. For E⊆F⊆L, localizing the integral scalar associator and then the E→L identification equals the F→L identification, T_L/F of the E→F identification, and the published rational alpha, in that order.

proof.text:
on complete integral objects use the finite-free completed scalar comparison
chi. Restrict it to the finite-Tor domain and apply Q. The rational scalar functor's
object and pure-tensor map clauses identify the resulting functor with T. Naturality
of chi makes these components a natural isomorphism; its components are precisely
Q(scalarBridge). CompletedScalarChainShift identifies the shift comparison with the
one fixed by scalarShift_existsUnique, first at degree one and then at every integer.
Exactness follows from integral exactness and the image triangulation of localization.
The identity normalization of chi gives the displayed scalar-unit equation.
ScalarCompletionAssociator identifies both three-field paths with the ordinary
balanced tensor associator. Applying Q and functoriality gives the displayed
composition equation, retaining the published alpha and unit.
